en: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani—and the wording is Yahya's—narrated to us; Yahya said: He informed us, and the other two said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever relieves a believer of one of the distresses of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the distresses of the Day of Resurrection. And whoever eases [the burden of] a person in financial difficulty, Allah will ease matters for him in this world and the Hereafter. And whoever conceals [the faults of] a Muslim, Allah will conceal him in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah continues to aid the servant as long as the servant is aiding his brother. And whoever traverses a path seeking knowledge therein, Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise. And no group of people gather in one of the houses of Allah reciting the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves except that tranquility descends upon them, mercy envelops them, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. And whoever is slowed down by his deeds will not be quickened by his lineage."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Marwan and 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Musa al-Juhani; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr—and the wording is his—narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Musa al-Juhani narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd: My father narrated to me, saying: We were in the company of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said: "Is one of you unable to earn one thousand good deeds every day?" A questioner from among his companions asked him: "How can one of us earn one thousand good deeds?" He said: "He glorifies Allah with one hundred glorifications (says Subhan Allah 100 times), and one thousand good deeds will be recorded for him, or one thousand misdeeds will be removed from him."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Abu Malik informed us, from his father, that he heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when a man came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should I say when I ask my Lord?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me well-being, and provide for me'"—and he drew his fingers together except for the thumb—"for these gather for you your worldly life and your Hereafter."

Sa'id ibn Azhar al-Wasiti narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: Abu Malik al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from his father, who said: Whenever a man embraced Islam, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would teach him the prayer, then command him to supplicate with these words: "O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me."

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us: Abu Malik al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to teach whoever embraced Islam to say: "O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, and provide for me."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Musa al-Juhani; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr—and the wording is his—narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Musa al-Juhani narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: A bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "Teach me words that I may say." He said: "Say: 'There is no god but Allah alone, having no partner; Allah is most great in great measure, and abundant praise is for Allah; glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; there is no power and no strength except by Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.'" He said: "These are for my Lord, so what is for me?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, and provide for me.'" Musa said: As for "grant me well-being" (wa 'afini), I suspect it, but I do not know for sure. And Ibn Abi Shaybah did not mention the statement of Musa in his hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "That I say: 'Subhan Allahi, wa al-hamdu lillahi, wa la ilaha illa Allahu, wa Allahu Akbar' (Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is most great) is more beloved to me than all over which the sun rises."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Abu Kurayb, and Muhammad ibn Tarif al-Bajali narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy in the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih, Subhan Allahil-'Azim' (Glory be to Allah and with His praise, Glory be to Allah the Magnificent)."

Sulayman ibn 'Ubaydullah Abu Ayyub al-Ghaylani narrated to us: Abu 'Amir—meaning al-'Aqadi—narrated to us: 'Umar—and he is Ibn Abi Za'idah—narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Whoever says ten times: 'There is no god but Allah alone, having no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent,' it is as if he emancipated four souls from the offspring of Isma'il." And Sulayman said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us: 'Umar narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Abi al-Safar narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, similar to that. He said: So I asked al-Rabi': "From whom did you hear it?" He said: "From 'Amr ibn Maymun." He said: So I came to 'Amr ibn Maymun and said: "From whom did you hear it?" He said: "From Ibn Abi Layla." He said: So I came to Ibn Abi Layla and said: "From whom did you hear it?" He said: "From Abu Ayyub al-Ansari narrating it from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Umawi narrated to me: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Suhayl, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever says when morning arrives and when evening arrives: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih' (Glory be to Allah and with His praise) one hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he has brought, except someone who said the like of what he said or increased upon it."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah alone, having no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent' one hundred times in a day, it shall be for him the equivalent of [freeing] ten slaves, one hundred good deeds will be recorded for him, one hundred misdeeds will be erased from him, and it will be a protection for him against Satan on that day of his until evening arrives; and no one will bring anything better than what he has brought except a person who did more than that. And whoever says: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih' (Glory be to Allah and with His praise) one hundred times in a day, his sins will be wiped away even if they were like the foam of the sea."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to say: "Rabbana atina fi al-dunya hasanatan wa fi al-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaba al-nar" (Our Lord, give us in this world what is good and in the Hereafter what is good, and protect us from the torment of the Fire).

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz—and he is Ibn Suhayb—who said: Qatadah asked Anas: "Which supplication did the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) make most often?" He said: The most frequent supplication he made was saying: "Allahumma atina fi al-dunya hasanatan wa fi al-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaba al-nar" (O Allah, give us in this world what is good and in the Hereafter what is good, and protect us from the torment of the Fire). He said: And whenever Anas wished to make a single supplication, he would supplicate with it; and whenever he wished to make a collection of supplications, he would include it therein.

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has roving angels who possess extra virtue, following the gatherings of remembrance. When they find a gathering wherein remembrance takes place, they sit with them and surround one another with their wings until they fill the space between them and the nearest heaven. When they disperse, they ascend and rise up to heaven. He said: So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, asks them, while He knows them best: 'From where have you come?' They say: 'We have come from some servants of Yours on earth who are glorifying You, declaring Your greatness, proclaiming Your oneness, praising You, and asking of You.' He says: 'And what are they asking Me for?' They say: 'They ask You for Your Paradise.' He says: 'And have they seen My Paradise?' They say: 'No, O Lord.' He says: 'How then if they had seen My Paradise?' They say: 'And they seek Your refuge.' He says: 'And from what do they seek My refuge?' They say: 'From Your Fire, O Lord.' He says: 'And have they seen My Fire?' They say: 'No.' He says: 'How then if they had seen My Fire?' They say: 'And they ask Your forgiveness.' He said: So He says: 'I have already forgiven them, granted them what they asked for, and granted them refuge from that which they sought refuge from.' He said: Then they say: 'O Lord, among them is so-and-so, a sinful servant who only passed by and sat down with them.' He said: So He says: 'And him too I have forgiven; they are the people whose companion shall not suffer misfortune on their account.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Salim ibn Nuh al-'Attar narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith.

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us: Thabit informed us, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered upon a man among his Companions to visit him while ill, and he had become like a fledgling bird... with the meaning of the hadith of Humayd, except that he said: "You have no endurance for the punishment of Allah." And he did not mention: "so he supplicated to Allah for him, and He healed him."

'Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi narrated it to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Humayd narrated to us with this chain of transmission up to his words: "and protect us from the torment of the Fire," and he did not mention the addition.

Abu al-Khattab Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) visited a man among the Muslims who had become so frail that he was like a fledgling bird. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Were you supplicating for anything or asking Him for it?" He said: "Yes, I used to say: 'O Allah, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.'" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Subhan Allah! You cannot endure it—or you cannot bear it—why did you not say: 'O Allah, give us in this world what is good and in the Hereafter what is good, and protect us from the torment of the Fire'?" He said: So he supplicated to Allah for him, and He healed him.
Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash with this chain of transmission, similar to it, except that he said: "then for him is ten the like thereof, or I increase."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like, and I increase [more]; and whoever comes with an evil deed, the recompense of an evil deed is an evil deed like it, or I forgive. And whoever draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; and whoever draws near to Me by an arm's length, I draw near to him by a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed; and whoever meets Me with sins near the capacity of the earth, without associating anything with Me, I will meet him with the like of it of forgiveness.'" Ibrahim said: Al-Hasan ibn Bishr narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us this hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him."
And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated it to us: Jarir informed me, from Mutarrif with this chain of transmission, similar to the hadith of 'Abthar.

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi narrated to us: 'Abthar informed us, from Mutarrif, from 'Amir, from Shurayh ibn Hani', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him." He said: So I came to 'A'ishah and said: "O Mother of the Believers, I heard Abu Hurayrah mentioning a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); if it is like that, then we are ruined." She said: "Indeed, the ruined one is the one ruined by the word of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). What is that?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "'Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him.' And there is none of us except that he dislikes death." She said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) indeed said it, but it is not as you understand it; rather, when the sight becomes fixed, the death rattle sounds in the chest, the skin shivers, and the fingers twitch—at that moment, whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him, and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us: Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Amir: Shurayh ibn Hani' narrated to me that 'A'ishah informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh ibn Hani', from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him, and death comes before meeting Allah."
Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Ruzzi narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith al-Hujaymi narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him." I said: "O Prophet of Allah, is it because of disliking death, for all of us dislike death?" He said: "It is not like that; rather, when the believer is given the glad tidings of Allah's mercy, His pleasure, and His Paradise, he loves meeting Allah, so Allah loves meeting him; and when the disbeliever is given the tidings of Allah's punishment and His wrath, he dislikes meeting Allah, so Allah dislikes meeting him."

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—so he mentioned several hadiths among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should wish for death, nor pray for it before it comes to him. Indeed, when one of you dies, his deeds come to an end, and verily the lifespan of a believer only increases him in good."
